The kokle is a Latvian plucked instrument of the Baltic box-zither or psaltery family, related to the Lithuanian kanklės, the Estonian kannel, the Finnish kantele and the Russian krylovidnye gusli, H-S number 314.122-5. The body is usually a hollow trapezoid carved from a single piece of wood and covered with a thin soundboard; the strings do not pass over a bridge, so the volume is smaller but the tone richer. The tuning pegs sit at the wide end, and at the narrow end the strings are fixed to a metal bar and fan out. It is played with the index finger of the right hand, the left hand damping or plucking; the Kurzeme type usually lies flat on the knees, while the Latgale type may stand on the knees. It is common in Latvian folk music, in music schools and amateur ensembles, and it is also used in modern folk, jazz and metal line-ups.
科克勒琴為彈撥弦鳴樂器，發聲靠手指撥弦，無琴橋使音量較小但音色較豐。初學可先依地: The kokle is a plucked chordophone: fingers pluck the strings, and the absence of a bridge makes it quieter but richer in tone. Begin by choosing a way of holding it that follows the regional tradition: the Kurzeme type usually rests flat on the knees, or on a table, while the Latgale type can sit more upright on the knees with its short edge against the belly and both arms around it. The right index finger sweeps the strings and the left hand touches the strings that should not sound in order to damp them, and may also pluck; the Latgale type also damps by threading the fingers between the strings, which restricts the left arm. The tuning is diatonic, and the lower strings may serve as drones.
科克勒琴為拉脫維亞弦鳴撥弦樂器，屬波羅的海箱形齊特琴家族。其演奏可於傳統民間音樂: The kokle is a Latvian plucked chordophone of the Baltic box-zither family. You can hear it in traditional folk settings, played sitting down or on a table in the Kurzeme and Latgale regions; it has also entered the concert world, as a solo instrument with folk ensembles, in conservatoires, music schools and amateur groups. Modern performance and recordings extend it to post-folk experiment, electro-folk, jazz improvisation and folk metal, which shows that it is not used only to accompany traditional songs.
科克勒琴為拉脫維亞撥弦樂器，屬波羅的海箱式齊特琴家族。拉脫維亞境內最早可能相關考: The kokle is a Latvian plucked instrument of the Baltic box-zither family. The earliest archaeological find in Latvia that may be related dates from the thirteenth century, and reliable written records begin in the early seventeenth century. The first tune notation appears in 1891, and records and film recordings followed in the 1930s. From the late nineteenth to the early twentieth century, under the influence of Central European zithers, a zither-style kokle appeared with a larger body and more strings. Modernised instruments appeared between the 1940s and 1960s; in 1951 the first large concert kokle was built, and it later entered conservatoires and amateur ensembles. After independence the Riga instrument factory closed, and production resumed in the mid-1990s.

Zither-style kokles use steel tuning pegs. Concert kokles were once made mainly from leftover piano materials. The source does not state the materials of other parts.
